applies_to: New Gemma policy rollout/branch sampling and deployment inference; not a relabeling of historical coldstart examples.

thinking.selection: Default2048; explicit1024/4096 profiles may use only current visible state and logical remaining budget. No reference-patch, oracle or future-outcome routing.

context.input_scope: Complete serialized prompt including system instructions, tool declarations, history, tool observations and generation prefix.
context.near_limit: When less space remains, the effective output cap must shrink or the request must end/undergo explicitly supported context management. No silent training-history truncation or claim that a full8192 remains available.
context.zero_remaining_space: No new generation request; record the actual context-limit outcome.

training_and_data_alignment.next_collection: Keep the600 task sources. Collect authentic thinking-enabled messages and outcomes under this new version; do not invent reasoning or simply flip historical prefix metadata.
training_and_data_alignment.prefix_note: Positive thinking tier values share the same initial template rendering only when all other inputs match; different generated histories are not identical states.
training_and_data_alignment.focal_pair_rule: Same-state original and alternative branches must use the same thinking tier, effective output cap, full prefix and logical remaining task budget. A budget-tier intervention is a separate experiment, not evidence of changing only one action.
training_and_data_alignment.long_rollout_training: New full32K trajectories require a separately supported trainer/window and actual memory measurement; preserve their complete states rather than silently truncating to12K.

accounting.per_task_cost: Accumulate all turns and the already-consumed prefix when branches are restored. Do not reset task budget or substitute CPU scripted-replay time for GPU policy inference time.

source_semantics.sampling_yaml_validation: Parsed as GenerateContentConfig on CPU; no server request or GPU execution.
